s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with localized erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels with plump endothelial cells
positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34
key_facts: female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
lesions are firm, nonscaly, and have irregular borders
no triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
no fever, weight loss, or fatigue
histopathological examination shows thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels
endothelial cells are plump but display no significant cytologic atypia
immunohistochemistry results are positive for CD31, CD34, and Ki-67 (<1%)
immunohistochemistry results are negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: possible match given the presence of plump endothelial cells and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and the lack of significant cytologic atypia

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: included due to the clinical presentation of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, although less common than other options

raw.rationale: The presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and plump endothelial cells without significant cytologic atypia, along with positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34, supports this diagnosis. The clinical presentation of firm, nonscaly, erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders also aligns with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: While tufted angioma can present with similar clinical features, the histopathological findings and immunohistochemistry results in this case are more consistent with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioma typically presents with more distinct epithelioid endothelial cells and a different immunohistochemical profile, which does not match the findings in this case.

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Retiform hemangioendothelioma is characterized by a retiform pattern of blood vessels, which is not described in the histopathological examination of this case.

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma typically presents with a distinctive targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition, which is not mentioned in the clinical presentation or histopathological findings of this case.
